device.candidatesNote: serial endpoints the agent found and has not been allowed to write to
device.candidatesHint: approving one lets the agent send AT to that port for an identity probe. A serial endpoint is not necessarily a modem — it can be a GPS, a debug console, or something that reboots when spoken to.
device.agentLogNote: the edge process's own output, most recent 500 lines, without an SSH session

device.apnHint: a username or password left alone keeps what the module holds; clearing one is the checkbox above
device.usbnetWarning: Any mode but rmnet takes effect at once, not at the next restart: the module re-enumerates on the spot, loses its QMI port, and disappears from the device list. Setting it back to rmnet from here brings it back.
device.confirmUsbnet: This mode takes effect immediately, not at the next restart. The module re-enumerates on the spot and loses its QMI control port — which is the port the agent finds it through, so it leaves the device list at once and stays out until somebody sets the mode back to rmnet.
device.confirmUsbnetRmnet: rmnet is the QMI mode this agent speaks, so the module finds its own way back into the device list. The switch is still an immediate re-enumeration: it disappears for tens of seconds, the console cannot reach it meanwhile, and connections running through it are cut.
device.diagNote: reads the module and the eUICC; changes nothing
device.modemNote: every control below is aimed at this one
device.atNote: typed commands go to the module's AT port untouched
device.ussdNote: the carrier's live menus: billable, and able to change the subscription
device.networkNote: manual operator selection, and what the module exposes over USB
device.dangerNote: each of these states its consequence before it asks
device.recoveryNote: the return leg for the two above; the console never sends it for you
device.logNote: the last 25, with whatever the device sent back
device.confirmRestartModem: Restarting this module resets its radio, its card and its USB together, and it leaves the device list for tens of seconds. The vowifi board's T078 recorded the time it did not come back: the module sat at +CFUN: 7, where AT+CFUN=0, =1 and =4 were all refused, and only a reset-form AT+CFUN=1,1 recovered it — on one observation. These modules arrive over USB/IP; nobody can walk over and replug one.
device.confirmResetModemUsb: This takes the module off the USB bus and lets it enumerate again. While it does, it is not in the device list and the console cannot reach it. If it does not come back, the only remaining move is restarting the edge host — nobody can get to this stick to replug it.
device.confirmScanOperators: The module serves nothing while a full-band sweep runs: no messages, no data, and any call on it drops. The edge gives the command 180 seconds and the module returns by itself afterwards with nothing for you to send — but for those three minutes it does nothing else.
device.confirmRotateIp: A new address is obtained by tearing the data bearer down and building it again: every connection currently running through this module is cut, the new address is whatever the carrier hands out, and the old one does not come back. It does not take the module off the network; messages and signalling are unaffected.
device.confirmRadioOff: With the radio off this module receives no messages, carries no data, drops any call on it, and shows as offline in the device list. The way back is the radio-on button in the recovery row; the console does not send it for you.
device.confirmDisableProfile: Leaves this module with no profile in service. It drops off the network until another one is enabled.
device.confirmDeleteProfile: Permanently removes this profile from the card. The card keeps no copy, and a profile that was paid for generally needs a fresh activation code from the operator to come back. This cannot be undone.
device.confirmClaimCandidate: Lets the agent send AT to this serial port for an identity probe. A serial endpoint is not necessarily a modem: it can be a GPS, a debug console, or something that reboots when spoken to.
device.confirmConfigureApn: Writes the APN context. The module keeps it across a reboot, so a wrong one takes this stick off data with no automatic way back.
device.confirmDataOff: Taking the data bearer down stops all traffic routed through this module, and the proxy exits behind it go with it. Messages and signalling stay up. The way back is the data-on button in the recovery row.
device.confirmReregister: Re-registering detaches and attaches again. The module is off the network in between, and when the network takes it back is the network's decision — usually seconds to a minute or so, with no guarantee, on a module nobody can restart by hand.
device.confirmSelectOperator: Manual selection pins this module to one PLMN. Locked to a network that is not on the air here, it searches for ever and stays off the network, while the page shows nothing worse than “searching”. The way back is the automatic button beside it, which the console does not press for you.
device.confirmUssdSend: A USSD code is a live instruction to the carrier: it can be billed, and it can change this SIM's subscription — call forwarding, bundles and value-added services all go this way. Nothing sent is recallable, and the line on the bill does not go away either.
device.confirmUssdReply: A menu item is a real choice rather than a page turn: confirming a purchase, switching call forwarding on and being charged are all done by replying with a digit. Nothing sent is recallable, and the menu text on screen was written by the carrier — the console cannot tell you what this item does.
device.confirmUnknownCommand: This console has no record of what this command does, so it cannot say what will happen. Until somebody writes the consequence down, treat it as one that cannot be undone.
device.atGuardUsbnet: On these EC20s AT+QCFG="usbnet" applies on the spot rather than at the next restart, and the module re-enumerates there and then. Every mode but rmnet(0) has no cdc-wdm QMI control port, and that port is how the agent finds a module — so this stick leaves the fleet immediately and stays out until somebody sets the mode back to 0, which can only be sent down another port.
device.atGuardCfunReset: The second parameter 1 is a reset: the module restarts and enumerates its USB again. These modules arrive over USB/IP with nobody able to touch them, so a reset that does not come back has no second route. The other half has to be said as well — on 2026-08-25, with a module stranded at +CFUN: 7, AT+CFUN=0, =1 and =4 all answered +CME ERROR: 4 and only this reset form recovered it, on a single observation.
device.atGuardCfunOff: This stick goes off the network at once: no messages, no data, any call on it drops, and it disappears from the device list for a while. For 0 and 4 the way back is AT+CFUN=1 on the same port. 7 is not like them — it is the value session.rs records as easy to enter and with every documented exit refused, and the one time this bench got a module out of 7 it took a reset-form AT+CFUN=1,1.
device.atGuardCops: AT+COPS=1 pins the module to one operator and =2 deregisters it. Locked to a network that is not on the air here it searches for ever, while the page shows nothing worse than “searching”; deregistered, it does not come back by itself. The way back is AT+COPS=0, which the console does not send for you. Note that the sweep, AT+COPS=?, is deliberately not in this table — it is slow, not irreversible.
device.atGuardCrsm: +CRSM hands a command straight to the card's own file system, and 214 / 219 / 220 are the writes. A corrupted EF has no undo, the card carries no second copy, and nobody can swap the card on this hardware. Reads are not guarded: the agent itself sends AT+CRSM=176 on every report.
device.atGuardCsim: +CSIM hands a whole APDU to the card verbatim, and the console cannot tell a read from a write inside one — so this entry has no read exception. The cost comes from this repository's own record: re-SELECTing the USIM ADF on a card that already had it selected made the card leave, after which every AT+CSIM answered +CME ERROR: 0 until an AT+CFUN=0 / 1 re-initialised it.
device.atGuardChannel: AT+CCHO opens, AT+CGLA uses and AT+CCHC closes: these are one operation, and closing is the other half rather than an option. An eUICC offers only three or four logical channels; once they are gone every later profile operation fails to open one, a leaked channel has no software way back, and nobody can replug this hardware. After closing, prove it: send one more AT+CGLA on the same session id and require it to fail — an OK from AT+CCHC is not evidence.
device.atGuardNvram: AT+QPRTPARA is Quectel's NV backup and restore. A factory NV reset erases things that have no second chance, and these modules arrive over USB/IP — if one does not come back afterwards there is no other route to it. The provenance is stated rather than dressed up: this command is in no source file in this repository. It comes from the vowifi board's T028, which listed it as an option with no physical access and no second chance, and did not run it.

proxy.title: Proxy
proxy.desc: Listeners that send traffic out over a chosen SIM.
proxy.configNote: desired state — the device applies it
proxy.confirmRemoveUpstream: The upstream “{name}” ({address}) is deleted permanently. {count} listener(s) point at it today and will fall back to a direct connection until you give them another upstream.
proxy.confirmRemoveInstance: The listener “{name}” ({listen}) and its configuration are deleted permanently. The device stops listening on that port, and every connection going through it drops at once.
proxy.confirmRemoveRule: The country rule {code} is deleted permanently. Cards from that country leave through the upstream “{upstream}” today; afterwards they fall back to each listener's own default route, which is usually a direct connection, until a rule is added again.
proxy.confirmStop: The listener “{name}” ({listen}) stops listening. Every connection going through it drops at once and clients are refused until it is started again. The configuration itself is kept.
proxy.confirmRestart: The listener “{name}” ({listen}) is stopped and started again. Every connection going through it drops, and new connections are refused while it comes back. This is not Start: starting a listener interrupts nothing.
proxy.trafficNote: as the device accounted for it
proxy.loadError: Proxy configuration could not be loaded.
proxy.exportNote: Connection strings contain the password. It is not shown on screen; Copy puts the complete string on the clipboard.
proxy.exportHostHint: Leave empty to use each listener's own configured address.
proxy.copyFailed: The browser refused to write to the clipboard; use an HTTPS page or copy by hand.
inbox.confirmDeleteThread: This permanently deletes the whole conversation with {peer} on the server, both directions, rather than hiding it here. It cannot be undone.
inbox.contactsNote: Name a number and it is used in the thread list and heading
inbox.confirmSend: This really sends a text message to {to} through device {device}. It is billed, and once it has gone it cannot be recalled or edited. The console picks the device; which module carries it is decided at the edge.
inbox.confirmDeleteMessage: This permanently deletes the message on the server rather than hiding it here, so it is gone for everyone who opens this conversation. It cannot be undone.
inbox.confirmForgetContact: This deletes the contact record for {peer} on the server. The thread list and the heading fall back to the bare number, and the name has to be typed again to get it back.
inbox.sendBlockedTitle: This device must not send text messages
inbox.sendBlockedDevice: This device carries a module that must not send, and this form picks a device rather than a module — with no module named the edge picks one, so sending from the whole device is switched off.
inbox.smsBlockedWhy: Module {imei}: every MO submit stalls its own QMI interrupt endpoint, the USB/IP session is torn down, and the module leaves the bus for tens of seconds. Both QMI and AT trigger it, and a full AT+CFUN=1,1 does not clear it.
inbox.smsBlockedCost: The cost is not a message that fails to go out: it usually does go out — the SIM's own MO counter in EF_SMSS advanced by 34 over a day of sends recorded as failures, and 10086 kept replying to them. The cost is losing the module every time.
inbox.smsModemsUnknownTitle: Sending is held: the module list could not be read
inbox.smsModemsUnknown: With the module list unread, whether this device carries the module that leaves the bus on every submit cannot be checked, so sending is held. Nothing went out and nothing is waiting to — reloading the page reads the list again, and sending comes back once it can be read.
cards.title: Card policies
cards.none: No card policies set. Cards without one use the device's defaults.
cards.confirmCellularOffTitle: Stop this card using cellular data
cards.confirmCellularOff: The policy is pushed to every device in this tenant at once: a module holding this card drops its cellular data connection and stays off until it is allowed again. Voice and SMS are not governed by this policy.
cards.confirmCellularOnTitle: Let this card use cellular data
cards.confirmCellularOn: The policy is pushed to every device in this tenant at once: a module holding this card dials up again, and the traffic it then carries is billed to this subscription.
cards.confirmVertical: The vertical decides which set of rules this card leaves the network under. The change reaches every device at once, and the data sessions in flight are dropped and re-established.
cards.confirmAddTitle: Give this card a policy of its own
cards.confirmAdd: This card stops following each device's defaults and follows this policy instead, on every device at once. It starts out with cellular data allowed and the cn vertical.
cards.confirmRemove: The policy is withdrawn from every device and the card falls back to each device's own cellular and vertical defaults. Adding it again restores those two, but the APN and the note do not come back.
journal.title: Journal
journal.note: newest first — expand a row for the envelope verbatim
journal.loadError: The journal could not be loaded.
device.name: Name
device.deleteNote: Removing a device deletes its entire journal, messages and commands. None of it can be recovered.
device.confirmDelete: Type the device name to confirm removal: {name}
esim.title: eSIM profiles
esim.none: No eUICC has reported its contents yet.
esim.renameNote: changes only the name stored on the card
esim.renameHint: blank clears the name; 64 bytes at most, and a Chinese character is three of them
esim.confirmSwitch: Switching disables the profile in use and enables the target one: the card is off the network across the re-registration, receiving no messages and carrying no data. A switch that half-lands can leave neither of them enabled, and nobody can pull this eUICC out to swap cards. Read the chip afterwards — the edge's switch reporting success is not the same as the card having changed.
esim.switchUnverified: The switch command answered “succeeded”, and nothing has read this chip since. Until it is read back, that is not evidence.
esim.switchConfirmed: Read back and confirmed: in the read taken after the switch, this ICCID is enabled.
esim.switchContradicted: Read back and contradicted: in the read taken after the switch, this ICCID is {state}, not enabled.
esim.noChip: No chip has been read yet. One button per module above; each press reads once.
esim.chipBusy: Command queued, waiting for the device to answer.
esim.profilesError: {imei}: this eUICC refused the profile list query, so the table below is not everything it holds
esim.chipReadFailed: {imei}: the last read of this eUICC failed
esim.notEuicc: {imei}: the card in this modem is not an eUICC. It refused to open an ISD-R channel, and every eUICC carries ISD-R, so there are no profiles to list. This is not a fault. The edge said:
esim.fCiVerify: GSMA CI keys it verifies against
esim.fCiSign: GSMA CI keys it signs with
esim.notDelivered: Not delivered to the SM-DP+ yet: {why}
esim.authTitle: ES9+ authentication (against a real SM-DP+, read-only)
esim.authNone: No SM-DP+ has been contacted yet. One button per module above.
esim.authBusy: Authentication queued, waiting for the device to answer.
esim.aSourceConfigured: the default SM-DP+ configured on the card
esim.aSourceNotification: a pending notification on the card
esim.checkCert: The GSMA CI root issued this SM-DP+ certificate
esim.checkChallenge: The echoed challenge is the one this chip just generated (not a replay)
esim.checkCiKey: The CI key the server chose is on this chip's verification list
esim.dlSecret: The activation code is sent with this one request. It is not written to the command log, to a log line, or back to this page.
esim.dlConfirm: Confirmation code (only if the SM-DP+ asks for one)
esim.dlWarn: This writes a profile into the eUICC and cannot be undone from here. It installs without enabling, so the profile carrying traffic now keeps the network. If the SM-DP+ attaches ppr1 or ppr2 - which would make the profile impossible to disable or delete, ever - the edge refuses and hands it back. The activation code is single-use and is spent by sending it, whether or not the install lands.
esim.dlBusy: Downloading and installing. An ES9+ round trip either side of a package fed to the card in blocks usually takes tens of seconds.
esim.dlNone: No profile has been downloaded yet.
esim.dlRefused: Refused: this profile carries {rules}, which cannot be removed once installed, and nobody can pull the eUICC out of the bench. Handed back to the SM-DP+ as SGP.22 provides.
esim.dlError: The eUICC refused the profile package
esim.dlNotEnabled: Not enabled (installing and enabling are two steps; only the first ran)
esim.dlNotifDelivered: Install notification delivered to the SM-DP+
esim.dlNotifRemoved: That notification removed from the card
settings.testFailed: The test could not be delivered.
settings.confirmTest: This sends a real notification through {channel} right now, using the credential the gateway is already holding, to whoever that channel is configured to reach. It cannot be recalled once it has gone out.
settings.confirmSave: Every field in the {section} section is written to the gateway as one document, for this whole tenant, replacing what is stored there now and taking effect immediately.
settings.confirmSaveSecrets: That includes the credential boxes: one you have typed into replaces the stored credential, and one you left empty keeps the stored one.
inbox.encoding8bit: Binary message (SIM toolkit / OTA), shown as hex
modems.unmanagedHint: The edge can only see this module over its AT port; QMI is unreachable, so it is visible but cannot be driven.
device.hostNote: The edge host itself, not the modules plugged into it
device.hostUnreported: This device has not reported host vitals yet.
device.radioNote: Signal readings as last reported by the edge
schedule.title: Scheduled tasks
schedule.desc: Recurring work addressed by device or by SIM: keep-alive messages, public IP checks. A task only advances while the tenant has a device connected.
schedule.loadError: Scheduled tasks could not be loaded.
empty.schedule.title: No scheduled tasks yet
empty.schedule.desc: A scheduled task issues a command on a cadence -- one keep-alive message to a service number, for instance. Create one with POST /v1/schedules.
rules.schedulesHint: Recurring work that runs without an operator lives here.
role.readOnlyDevice: Read-only account: this device can be watched, not operated.
role.readOnlySettings: Read-only account: settings are shown but cannot be changed. Your own password still can be.
role.readOnlyInbox: Read-only account: messages can be read. Sending, deleting and renaming are not available.
role.readOnlyCards: Read-only account: card policies can be read. Adding, removing and changing them are not available.

pwa.install.title: Install the console
pwa.install.hint: It opens full screen, without the browser's address bar.
pwa.install.iosHint: In Safari, tap Share at the bottom, then Add to Home Screen.
connection.stale: the data on screen is from
device.atForceHint: The agent refuses AT commands that change radio, call, message, card or persistent configuration state. Tick to send one anyway. Clears after each send.
cards.confirmCapabilityOff: The edge will stop attempting this operation on this card and will refuse it with the reason that the plan does not include it. Nothing about the module or the network changes.
cards.confirmCapabilityOnTitle: Record the plan as including this?
cards.confirmCapabilityOn: The card stops withholding this operation, so the edge attempts it whenever the module and network were measured to support it. It grants nothing on its own.
cards.confirmCapabilityClear: The declaration returns to undeclared, which withholds nothing: the module and the network decide alone until somebody records the plan again.
cards.capabilityHint: What the plan on this card is sold as doing. Only \u201cnot included\u201d changes anything: it withholds the operation. It can never grant one the module and network were not measured to have.
ledger.title: Support ledger
ledger.desc: What has been measured, on which module, on whose network. A pairing that is not here is refused by the edge as untested.
ledger.measuredNote: Each row is a claim somebody made on a particular day. The edge routes by these and by nothing else.
ledger.emptyDesc: Until a pairing is recorded here the edge refuses it, naming the missing measurement. That is the intended state for a fleet nobody has tested yet, not a fault.
ledger.loadFailed: The ledger could not be read, so this page cannot say what is supported.
ledger.recordNote: Saving changes nothing about what the fleet attempts. Publishing does.
ledger.publishNote: Publishing replaces what every device routes by. A pairing that has fallen out of the ledger stops working the moment it lands.
ledger.confirmPublishTitle: Publish the ledger to every device?
ledger.confirmPublish: Every device in this tenant is given this ledger and starts routing by it immediately, replacing what it holds. Any pairing not recorded here stops working, including ones that work today.
modems.uncharacterisedHint: the ledger holds no rule for this (family, carrier) pair: not unsupported, just never measured
modems.apnHint: The packet data profiles on the module itself, as AT+CGDCONT? reports them. Which one carries data is a row on the module, not a property of the card.
